show_hn.story_text: I have been exploring a different future for AI where we can finally take control of our models and keep our data 100% private. I built modelXare with the goal of creating the DNS-equivalent for AI capabilities. It uses a combination of system one and system two models to dynamically route the user intent(s) to the ideal micro-model(s) that gets downloaded (and cached) locally to processes your request. This is just the first iteration of this vision. There is a lot of work that needs to be done and a lot of micro-models that can be added but imagine a world where we all can build this network of micro-models together and break the chains from the big AI labs.

show_hn.story_text: Ribbon Architect is available as a free iOS app and in the browser. Scan or measure a gift, browse pattern suggestions made for its exact proportions, or construct your own designs. Then step-by-step instructions show you how to lay the ribbon on your gift. Gifts are modeled as convex polyhedra, so many non-cuboid gift shapes, such as prisms, work too and have their own interesting ribbon patterns. A ribbon (without twists) that is pulled tight follows a locally shortest path, a geodesic. This is a path on the surface of the gift that runs straight on faces and folds correctly over edges and loops back on itself. As you'll see in the app, geodesics can be much more interesting than the axis-aligned loops that people usually tie when wrapping a gift. Click "Browse geodesics"

show_hn.story_text:
137 file types; a single file with nothing to install.
Introducing Provost, the free compression and archival tool that can create 119 formats, and open 137 total.  It's new custom format packs smaller than ZPAQ, xz, and Zstandard in tests.
JPEG, PNG, PDF, DOCX/XLSX, and gzip are unpacked and repacked for ~25% smaller files; ability to encrypt to people's keys or a password; can open archives straight from HTTPS, S3, WebDAV, and SFTP; can search inside archives, including the text of Office files and PDFs; and much more. Q&A
---
Is it open source?
 It is not. Will my .provost files open in five years?
 I've committed to future releases reading every 0.1.0 archive, and to old compression methods staying readable. Are builds signed?
 No. The Mac app isn't notariz

Show HN: Budget – an open-source private budgeting app for Mac and Windows
show_hn.story_text: Budget is a free, open-source app for Mac and Windows. With the simple mode, it gives you what you'd expect of a budgeting app: configure budgets and track expenses against those budgets. But, if you're a geek like me and are way too interested in your personal finance, the extended mode offers features like carrying leftover budgets to the next month, splitting expenses across multiple budgets and seeing how much you can freely spend the coming year, while taking into account any large future expenses (like a car insurance where the premium is paid on a yearly basis). This app is the result of a hobby of mine to track my expenses. It started a few years ago in a spreadsheet, but that spreadsheet at some point took me minutes to edit on my MacBook with 8 gigs of RAM. I had the id

show_hn.title: Show HN: Ding – Toast notifications that morph instead of stacking
show_hn.story_text: I've been working on a toast library called Ding. I wanted to try something different from the usual stacked notifications. When a new toast appears, it can take over the previous one with a spring animation instead of adding another toast to the screen. It works with React, Svelte 5, Vue and vanilla JS. It's still something I'm improving, so I'd be happy to hear what you think. Source: https://github.com/YusufCeng1z/ding
